subject: ventures/job-application-tracker
professional: a career coach who runs job-search programmes (follow-up cadence, tracking response rate by channel), with a senior web engineer's eye on CSV import/export (RFC 4180, OWASP CSV injection) and calendar export (RFC 5545)

evidence.correctness: node -e on tracker.mjs: applied 2026-11-01 -> follow-up 2026-11-08 (7-day rule); screen on 2026-11-10 -> follow-up 2026-11-13 and first response 9 days; quiet flag at exactly 30 days (12-01) and not at 29 (11-30); 2028-02-28 + 1 = 2028-02-29 and 2026-02-29 rejected (Gregorian calendar by hand); funnel of 2 apps, 1 reply = 50%, median 9 days; CSV export prefixes '=HYPERLINK' and '-2+3' with a quote and round-trips '=SUM(A1)' and '@x'.
evidence.completeness: README features checked: follow-up defaults and override, quiet-after-30-days suggestion, reply rate by source, CSV export with formula guard, CSV/JSON import with duplicate skipping (index.html:235-242), .ics download. All present and working. No stubs.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 37 pass. quality_mutate.py: 5 mutants, 2 survived: the nextActions horizon boundary (>= -> >) and dropping '-' from the CSV-injection prefix set, the second a security rule.
evidence.craft: tracker.mjs (253 lines) read in full: pure functions, dates passed in, RFC 4180 quoting in parseCsv handles CRLF, BOM and doubled quotes. Defects: .ics lines are not folded at 75 octets (a long company+role SUMMARY reached 159 characters; RFC 5545 3.1); DTSTAMP defaults to a fixed 20260101T000000Z and index.html:228-230 never passes a real stamp; Number('120,000') silently drops a comma-formatted salary on import.
evidence.claims: README claims (7/3-day defaults, 30-day quiet, rejection counts as a reply, formula guard on = + - @, import column names, local-only storage) each match tracker.mjs. The vs-a-spreadsheet page states 'dates as YYYY-MM-DD'. Disclaimer present on the page (index.html, footer) and README.
evidence.fitness: Walked a week of a job search: add 6 applications from 3 sources, move two to screen, export .ics, export CSV, re-import. Works, but a sheet re-saved by a spreadsheet turns dates into 11/20/2026 and the import blanks them with no message, so a user moving from a spreadsheet loses every date without being told.
evidence.domain: Follow-up gaps (about a week after applying, a few days after an interview) match common career-coaching guidance, and the guide calls them conventions. The CSV formula guard follows OWASP's CSV Injection list (= + - @ tab CR). The departure is RFC 5545 line folding and DTSTAMP.

checks.what: follow-up 3 days after a screen, first response in days
CSV formula guard on export and strip on import
checks.expected: quoted on export, restored on import
salary 120000, a warning about the date
checks.observed: salary null, applied blank, no warning

mutations.change: drop '-' from the CSV-injection prefix set

defects.what: Dropping '-' from the CSV-injection guard leaves every test green: the security rule the README advertises is untested for one of its four characters. The horizon boundary in nextActions also survives.
CSV import blanks dates not in YYYY-MM-DD (what a spreadsheet re-save produces) and drops '120,000' or '$120,000' salaries, with no message, so a spreadsheet migration silently loses data.
.ics content lines are not folded at 75 octets (RFC 5545 3.1); a long company and role made a 159-character SUMMARY line.
DTSTAMP is a fixed 20260101T000000Z because the page never passes a stamp; RFC 5545 expects the time the object was created.

verdict: A careful little tracker: nine outputs recomputed by hand all pass, the README matches the code claim by claim, and the CSV formula guard follows OWASP. It misses the bar only on verification: 2 of 5 seeded mutants survived, one of them in the CSV-injection rule. The worst user-facing gap is a spreadsheet re-import that silently blanks dates and comma-formatted salaries. This round adds tests that kill both mutants, reads '$120,000' salaries and reports how many rows had dates it could not read. .ics folding and DTSTAMP are still open.
